koreterm 1.3.143

- Remote Desktop tabs: right-click the tab, "Run Command on Remote
  Desktop...". Type a command (or pick Explorer, Processes, Services,
  Events or Restart) and send it to the remote computer's Run box, to a
  PowerShell window on its screen, or to PowerShell on the server through
  WinRM, which shows whether it ran and its output. "Open Task Manager"
  works even when the remote Explorer is gone. A restart or shutdown is
  asked about first.
- An applied update.zip is deleted, also when it was still in use while
  the update ran.

koreterm 1.3.142

- Settings > Profiles: "Sort A to Z" lists the profiles alphabetically;
  "Picker order" shows them again in the order of the profile menu (the
  arrow beside the tabs), the order Move up and Move down change.
- Settings > Profiles: "Hide built-in profiles" lists only the profiles you
  made; the ones koreterm finds (PowerShell, Command Prompt, WSL, SSH hosts)
  come back with "Show built-in profiles". Their rows now have a tinted
  background, so your own stand apart.
- Each profile has Notes: free text, any number of lines, in the profile
  window (Settings > Profiles > Edit). They are saved with the profile and
  never passed to the shell.

koreterm 1.3.141

- noctty is now koreterm, with a new icon: a core linked to its connections.
  The program is koreterm.exe; your config.ghostty and saved passwords stay
  where they are.
- Remote Desktop tabs no longer drop when left idle: the session now sends a
  keep-alive every minute. After a network drop the tab reconnects by itself
  at most twice, 15 seconds apart, and a login that fails is never retried,
  so a saved password that went stale cannot lock your account. When a
  session really ends, the tab says so.
- Remote Desktop no longer asks about a server whose certificate cannot be
  checked: connecting without asking is now the default. Settings > Shell has
  "Remote Desktop unverified server" to change it, and each RDP connection's
  editor can set its own.
- New in the window menu (the arrow beside the tabs): "Create Desktop and
  Start Menu Shortcuts" puts a koreterm shortcut on the Desktop and in the
  Start menu.
- A profile opened as administrator now starts in its own starting folder,
  not in the folder of the tab it was opened from.
- Tabs show their profile's icon: the program's own icon by default, or one
  you choose in the profile window (Settings > Profiles > Edit): a .ico,
  .exe or .dll file, an emoji, or none. The same window sets a tab color,
  drawn as a stripe along the top of the tab.
- A new tab, from the + button or a profile, now opens after the last tab
  (window-new-tab-position = current brings back the old place).
- A variable set with setx (or in System Properties) now reaches the next
  tab you open, as it does in a new window from the Start menu.
